name: heretic
description: Training-free language model modification: Remove censorship, suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more
one_liner: A tool that edits an existing AI model's behavior — like removing its refusals or reducing its corporate-sounding filler — without retraining it, on a home gaming PC.
buyer: A niche and ethically mixed market: hobbyists running uncensored local chatbots, and AI safety or red-team researchers probing how easily a model's guardrails come off.
business_use_cases: An AI red-team researcher uses it to stress-test how robust a model's safety training actually is before recommending it for deployment.
A hobbyist publishes a 'spicier' fine-tune of an open model for a local-AI enthusiast community — an ethically contested use case, not a storefront to build on.
A benchmark author uses the 'suppress slop' and 'reduce sycophancy' modes to produce more natural-sounding outputs for research, separate from censorship removal.

money_ideas.idea: Paid red-team and robustness-testing services for companies deploying open models, using this as part of the toolkit.

steal_this: The legitimate weekend build here is a safety-testing report generator for open-weight models, not an uncensored-chatbot product — the censorship-removal use case carries real reputational and platform risk and shouldn't be the business.
